reconstruction_note: The blog post was published 2026-06-29 from a firsthand run whose original harness scripts (run_experiments.py / feature_matrix.py / round2.py) and their .txt logs were deleted after publish per firsthand-cleanup policy; only the summary firsthand-benchmark.md survived. This run dir is NOT a paper backfill: the deterministic parts (the 6-version bisect and the behavioral experiments) were RE-RUN live on 2026-08-04 by re-downloading the six pinned sqlite-tools binaries from sqlite.org. Every recorded verdict was reproduced exactly. Only the hardware-specific timing/large-table experiments (3M/5M rows) from the original run are not re-measured -- see results.json not_measured.

environment.runner: precompiled sqlite3.exe CLI, no Docker, no network at run time
environment.note: This is a SQL-parser capability + DDL-behavior check, not a timing benchmark. Fixed schemas + pinned CLI builds produce fixed OK/ERR verdicts and fixed stderr; CPU/RAM do not affect the result, so they are omitted.

subject.name: sqlite
subject.feature: ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN (SET/DROP NOT NULL, ADD/DROP CHECK constraint)
subject.install: download the pinned sqlite-tools zips listed in run.sh from https://sqlite.org/ (win-x64 3480000..3530000; year dir 2025 for 3.48-3.51, 2026 for 3.52-3.53)
subject.verified_via: each sqlite3.exe reported its own version string (e.g. '3.52.0 2026-03-06 ...') before probing

raw_artifacts.retention_policy: none discarded -- all evidence is small and committed
raw_artifacts.note: feature_matrix.py, experiments.py, and the deterministic probe-result.json are committed. The six ~6.4 MB sqlite-tools zips were downloaded, executed, and deleted after the run (firsthand cleanup); run.sh re-fetches the same pinned versions to reproduce.
